newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa appeals for calm after Mideast shooting.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa appeals for calm after Mideast shooting.

text.p: South Africa appealed for calm in the Middle East on Thursday after a Jordanian soldier shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls, cautioning that there was a "grave danger" that the current crisis could be manipulated.
"An appeal is made to all sides to abide by their commitment to seek a negotiated peace in the region," the Foreign Affairs department said in a statement.

"One of the grave dangers of the current crisis is that it provides a pretext to those opposed to peace to exploit widespread perceptions that the present Likud-led government is not seriously committed to the quest for a just and equitable solution to the problems of the region."
Pretoria also revealed that Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had raised similar concerns with its envoys, saying:
"In fact, President Arafat signalled his concern in this regard during discussions with an official South African delegation which visited Palestine during the past weekend."

Foreign Affairs gave no details of the talks but the South African government, which under apartheid had close trade and military ties with Israel, has also developed close relations with the Palestinian Authority since white rule ended in 1994.

The seven Israeli teenagers were killed when a Jordanian soldier sprayed automatic weapon fire at a school group before being disarmed by fellow soldiers. South Africa condemned the attack as "senseless".
